```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
```

orbital translates fitted `mlp()` parsnip models from the `"brulee"` and
`"keras"` / `"keras3"` engines into SQL column expressions that reproduce
the model's predictions row-by-row.  No Python or PyTorch process is needed
at inference time — the SQL is self-contained.

## Quick start

```r
library(parsnip)
library(orbital)

# Fit a brulee MLP
spec <- mlp(hidden_units = c(32, 16), activation = "relu", epochs = 50) |>
  set_engine("brulee") |>
  set_mode("regression")

fit <- spec |> fit(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)

# Translate to SQL column expressions
orb <- orbital(fit)
orb

# Apply to in-memory data with dplyr
library(dplyr)
mtcars_tbl <- as_tibble(mtcars)
predict(orb, new_data = mtcars_tbl)
```

---

## Supported layer types

The table below summarises which keras3 / keras layer types orbital can
translate.

| Layer type | orbital support | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Dense` | ✅ Supported | Full `W·x + b` with output activation |
| `BatchNormalization` | ✅ Supported | Inference constants (mean, var, γ, β) frozen at export |
| `LayerNormalization` | ✅ Supported | Per-row symbolic mean and variance expressions |
| `PReLU` | ✅ Supported | Per-channel learnable negative slopes |
| `ELU` | ✅ Supported | Alpha extracted from layer config |
| `LeakyReLU` | ✅ Supported | Alpha extracted from layer config |
| `GELU` | ✅ Supported | `0.5·x·(1 + tanh(√(2/π)·(x + 0.044715·x³)))` approximation |
| `ReLU` / `Activation("relu")` | ✅ Supported | Standard `max(0, x)` |
| `Sigmoid` / `Activation("sigmoid")` | ✅ Supported | `1 / (1 + exp(-x))` |
| `Tanh` / `Activation("tanh")` | ✅ Supported | `(exp(2x)-1)/(exp(2x)+1)` |
| `Softmax` | ✅ Supported | Stable log-sum-exp normalisation |
| `Activation("elu")` | ✅ Supported | |
| `Activation("selu")` | ✅ Supported | `scale * (x ≥ 0 ? x : alpha·(exp(x)-1))` |
| `Activation("gelu")` | ✅ Supported | |
| `Dropout` | ✅ Pass-through | Identity at inference time |
| `Concatenate` | ✅ Supported | axis=1 (feature concat) only |
| `Add` (residual) | ✅ Supported | Element-wise sum of two input branches |
| `GlobalAveragePooling1D` | ✅ Supported | Row-wise mean over all input features |
| `GlobalMaxPooling1D` | ✅ Supported | Row-wise max over all input features |
| `InstanceNormalization` | ✅ Supported | Per-row mean and variance (same formula as LayerNorm) |
| `GroupNormalization` | ✅ Supported | `num_groups=1` → LayerNorm; `num_groups=n_features` → per-feature |
| `LSTM` / `GRU` / `RNN` | ❌ Not supported | Recurrent layers are not translatable to SQL |
| `Conv1D` / `Conv2D` | ❌ Not supported | Requires spatial aggregation |
| `GlobalAveragePooling2D/3D` | ❌ Not supported | Requires spatial aggregation |
| `Attention` / `MultiHeadAttention` | ❌ Not supported | |

## Example 1 — Sequential model with BatchNorm and ELU

```r
library(keras3)
library(parsnip)
library(orbital)

# Build and compile the model
inp   <- layer_input(shape = 4)
out   <- inp |>
  layer_dense(16) |>
  layer_batch_normalization() |>
  layer_activation_elu(alpha = 1.0) |>
  layer_dense(1)

model <- keras_model(inp, out)
model |> compile(optimizer = "adam", loss = "mse")
model |> fit(matrix(rnorm(800), 200, 4), rnorm(200), epochs = 10, verbose = 0)

# Wrap in a parsnip fit and translate
fit   <- keras3_mlp_fit(model, mode = "regression", feature_names = paste0("x", 1:4))
orb   <- orbital(fit)
orb
#> ── orbital Object ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 4 equations in total.
#> ...

# Score new data — pure dplyr, no Python required
library(dplyr)
new_data <- tibble(x1 = 0.1, x2 = -0.5, x3 = 1.2, x4 = 0.3)
predict(orb, new_data)
```

---

## Example 2 — Functional API with Concatenate

```r
library(keras3)
library(parsnip)
library(orbital)

# Two input branches merged with Concatenate
branch_a <- layer_input(shape = 3)
branch_b <- layer_input(shape = 3)

out <- layer_concatenate(list(branch_a, branch_b)) |>
  layer_dense(8, activation = "relu") |>
  layer_dense(1)

model <- keras_model(list(branch_a, branch_b), out)
model |> compile(optimizer = "adam", loss = "mse")

x_a <- matrix(rnorm(300), 100, 3)
x_b <- matrix(rnorm(300), 100, 3)
y   <- rnorm(100)
model |> fit(list(x_a, x_b), y, epochs = 10, verbose = 0)

# orbital handles multi-input Functional models
fit <- keras3_mlp_fit(
  model, mode = "regression",
  feature_names = c(paste0("a", 1:3), paste0("b", 1:3))
)
orb <- orbital(fit)
```

---

## Example 3 — GlobalAveragePooling1D

```r
library(keras3)
library(parsnip)
library(orbital)

inp <- layer_input(shape = 8)
out <- inp |>
  layer_dense(8, activation = "relu") |>
  layer_global_average_pooling_1d() |>   # reduces 8 features → 1 mean
  layer_dense(1)

model <- keras_model(inp, out)
model |> compile(optimizer = "adam", loss = "mse")
model |> fit(matrix(rnorm(800), 100, 8), rnorm(100), epochs = 5, verbose = 0)

fit <- keras3_mlp_fit(model, mode = "regression", feature_names = paste0("x", 1:8))
orb <- orbital(fit)
```

## brulee models

`brulee` uses PyTorch under the hood; orbital extracts weights and activation
function names directly from the fitted Torch module.

```r
library(parsnip)
library(orbital)

# Fit a brulee MLP with ELU activation
spec <- mlp(hidden_units = c(32, 16), activation = "elu", epochs = 50) |>
  set_engine("brulee") |>
  set_mode("regression")

fit <- spec |> fit(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)
orb <- orbital(fit)

# The ELU alpha is extracted automatically from the Torch module
orb
```

### Supported brulee activations

All activations listed in `brulee::mlp()` are supported:
`relu`, `tanh`, `sigmoid`, `elu`, `selu`, `gelu`, `leaky_relu`,
`softplus`, `silu` / `swish`, and `mish`.

The `leaky_relu` negative slope and `elu` / `celu` alpha are extracted
automatically from the fitted `torch::nn_module` — you do not need to pass
them manually.

---

## Known limitations

### SQL expression depth
Deep networks (6+ hidden layers, 100+ units per layer) produce very long SQL
strings.  Some databases impose limits on query-string length or query-plan
depth.  For very deep models, consider materialising intermediate layer outputs
into temporary tables.

### Spatial layers
`GlobalAveragePooling2D`, `GlobalMaxPooling2D`, `Conv1D`, `Conv2D`, and
similar spatial layers are not supported.  Only 1-D feature inputs (a single
flat vector per row) are translatable to SQL.

### Recurrent and attention layers
`LSTM`, `GRU`, `RNN`, `MultiHeadAttention`, and related layers require
sequential state that cannot be expressed as a SQL column expression.

### GroupNorm with arbitrary groups
`GroupNormalization` with `num_groups` other than 1 or `n_features` raises
an error because intermediate group-statistics cannot be expressed as a
single SQL expression without temporary tables.

### Runtime dependencies at fit time
keras3 models require a working Python + TensorFlow/JAX/PyTorch backend to
*fit* the model.  Once the orbital object is created no Python process is
needed — all prediction SQL is self-contained.

### H2O Maxout
The Maxout activation uses a grouped max-pooling architecture that orbital
does not currently support.  Use `Rectifier`, `Tanh`, or `Sigmoid` for
orbital-compatible H2O models.
